intro: A broken garage door spring stops your day. When your garage door won't open, or if you heard a loud bang from the garage, a spring is likely the cause. We provide fast, reliable garage door spring repair for Evanston homeowners. Our technicians fix broken torsion and extension springs across town, from Central Street to South Evanston. We arrive with common parts stocked on our trucks. You get an upfront, flat-rate quote before any work begins. Our family-owned business offers dispatch 24 hours a day, Monday through Saturday, for emergency spring repairs. Get your garage door operating safely again with our experienced local service.
localContext: Evanston's location off Lake Michigan means garage door springs work harder here. Lake-effect snow, persistent winds, and salt air increase corrosion on metal components. This includes the springs, cables, and bearings. Rust and fatigue can cause premature spring failure. Many homes in areas like the Ridge Historic District feature century-old detached garages. These older structures, often accessed via rear alleys, may have original garage door hardware. The weight of older, heavier carriage-house style doors, common due to historic district rules, adds stress to springs. We know Evanston's garage doors and the specific challenges they face from our local climate and housing stock.

problemSigns.detail: Often indicates a broken torsion spring.

problemSigns.sign: Garage door won't lift or feels extremely heavy
problemSigns.detail: A broken spring means the opener struggles with the door's full weight.

problemSigns.sign: Visible gap in the torsion spring above the door
problemSigns.detail: A clear sign of a broken torsion spring.

problemSigns.sign: Garage door lifts a few inches then stops
problemSigns.detail: The door opener's safety system detects imbalance from a broken spring.

problemSigns.sign: Cables look loose or slack on the drum
problemSigns.detail: Indicates a loss of tension from a broken spring.
